title: Customs and Other Legislation Amendment Bill 2016
short_title: Customs and Other Legislation Amendment Bill 2016

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would amend customs administration, export permit controls and trade description rules, and clarify maritime enforcement powers during passage through another country’s waters.
It would permit export licence revocation on security, defence or international relations grounds and remove the mandatory interim stage of Australian Trusted Trader agreements.
Most schedules would begin the day after Royal Assent, with later commencement arrangements for export controls and the trusted trader changes.
changes: The minister could exempt specified importers or goods from import declaration processing charges.
The manufacturing history period relevant to made-to-order capital equipment tariff concessions would extend from two years to five.
Trade description regulations could prescribe offence penalties up to 50 penalty units.
Maritime powers could be exercised during passage through foreign waters consistent with the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea.
summary.affected: Importers, exporters, trusted traders, Australian manufacturers and maritime officers are affected.

speeches.speaker: Peter Dutton
speeches.brief: The Customs and Other Legislation Amendment Bill 2016 proposes amendments to allow the Defence Minister to revoke export permits for defence and strategic goods if they would prejudice national security, streamline the Australian Trusted Trader program by removing interim status agreements, exempt certain parties from import declaration processing charges, permit opening sealed duty-free bags for rescreening, remove the 25% factory cost test for manufacturers, extend the evidentiary window for made-to-order capital equipment from two to five years, and confirm Maritime Powers Act powers consistent with UNCLOS.

speeches.speaker: Shayne Neumann
speeches.brief: The speaker announced Labor's support for the Customs and Other Legislation Amendment Bill 2016, which amends three acts to allow exemptions from import processing charges, enable duty-free bag screening at airports, remove the 25% factory cost test for tariff concession objections, extend the evidentiary window for made-to-order capital equipment from two to five years, and confirm maritime powers under UNCLOS.

speeches.speaker: Alan Tudge
speeches.brief: The Customs and Other Legislation Amendment Bill 2016 amends the Customs Act, Commerce (Trade Descriptions) Act, and Maritime Powers Act, including allowing the defence minister to revoke export permits for security or international relations reasons, streamlining trusted trader accreditation, and clarifying maritime powers under the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea.
